stories.why: Nvidia is a central player in the global semiconductor and artificial intelligence markets, making its leadership stability critical for investor sentiment in the tech sector.

stories.headline: US Crude Export Hub Corpus Christi Faces Frequent Cyberattacks
stories.summary: The Port of Corpus Christi, which handles nearly 60% of US crude oil exports, faces thousands of daily cyberattack attempts. Port officials reported an escalation in attacks against shipping and port systems.
stories.why: The Port of Corpus Christi is the principal gateway for crude oil exports from the United States to international markets.

stories.headline: Madison Dearborn Partners to Acquire Peli BioThermal
stories.summary: Madison Dearborn Partners has agreed to acquire Peli BioThermal from Pelican Products and Platinum Equity. The deal provides strategic capital to accelerate the healthcare supply chain provider's global growth.
stories.why: Peli BioThermal is a significant provider of cold chain solutions for the pharmaceutical industry, a sector that has seen increased M&A activity due to complex logistics requirements.

stories.headline: Financial inclusion in Mexico: how it varies between states and municipalities
stories.summary: The 2026 Banamex Financial Inclusion Index confirms a territorial gap in access to and use of banking services across Mexico. CDMX, Baja California Sur and Nuevo León lead the ranking.
stories.why: Financial inclusion measures how many people use formal banking services, which affects the potential growth of credit and payments markets for banks.
stories.original_headline: La inclusión financiera en México: así cambia entre estados y municipios

stories.headline: Sánchez, Feijóo and Abascal: three protagonists of the Spanish elections
stories.summary: Pedro Sánchez, the conservative Alberto Núñez Feijóo and the far-right Santiago Abascal are the main contenders seeking to become Spain's prime minister.
stories.why: Spain is the euro area's fourth-largest economy, and the outcome of its elections can influence fiscal policy, regulation and Spanish government bond markets.
stories.original_headline: Sánchez, Feijóo y Abascal: tres protagonistas de las elecciones españolas

stories.headline: PSEi regains ground after steep sell-off
stories.summary: The PSEi rose 0.87% to close at 5,353.07 after touching an intraday high of 5,419.49, rebounding from a steep sell-off the previous week. Trading remained light and the index failed to hold above 5,400.
stories.why: The PSEi is the benchmark index of the Philippine Stock Exchange, tracking the country's largest listed companies and serving as a gauge of local market sentiment.

stories.headline: Sheinbaum denies that Trump spoke about the cartels at the APEC meeting
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said her bilateral meeting with Donald Trump at APEC focused exclusively on trade matters. She attributed Trump's remarks on cartels to an earlier phone call.
stories.why: Trade and security relations between Mexico and the United States shape tariffs, supply chains and investor sentiment toward Mexico.
stories.original_headline: Sheinbaum niega que Trump hablara de los cárteles en reunión de la APEC

stories.headline: The Jeep Recon is already being produced in Mexico for our market, days before its presentation
stories.summary: The first Jeep Recon, an electric Jeep with Trail Rated certification, has been built in Mexico for the local market. The first unit for Mexico has left the production line in Toluca.
stories.why: Stellantis is a global automaker, and local production of new models in Mexico reflects its manufacturing footprint and supply chain in the country.
stories.original_headline: El Jeep Recon ya se produce en México para nuestro mercado, a días de su presentación

stories.headline: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest Abandons Plans for Two Crypto ETFs
stories.summary: ARK Invest has withdrawn its applications for two planned cryptocurrency ETFs. The decision comes as rival crypto funds have registered modest asset growth following their launch.
stories.why: ARK Investment Management is an asset management firm specializing in innovation-focused thematic exchange-traded funds.

stories.headline: Senegal: Impeachment for high treason, a constitutional weapon without ammunition
stories.summary: The PASTEF party is seeking impeachment of Senegal's head of state for high treason ahead of a resolution on a 19 November 2026 budget decree. The article notes the outcome will depend on the ballot box.
stories.why: Budget decrees set public spending and fiscal targets, so political conflict over them can affect sovereign credit perceptions and debt markets.
stories.original_headline: Sénégal : Mise en accusation pour Haute trahison, une arme constitutionnelle sans munition

stories.headline: Dominican Republic Christmas Bonus and requirements to access it
stories.summary: The Dominican government announced eligibility requirements for a 1,500-peso Christmas bonus. It will reach 2,753,781 people and families through direct transfers and cards distributed by community organizations.
stories.why: Direct cash transfers from the state add to household spending power in the Dominican Republic, and government social spending is a component of the public budget.
stories.original_headline: Bono Navideño República Dominicana y requisitos para acceder

stories.headline: Drone Attacks and Storms Disrupt Russian Crude Oil Exports
stories.summary: Russian crude oil shipments from the Baltic and Black seas face loading delays due to severe weather and Ukrainian drone attacks. Delays have affected more than 10 oil tankers at Baltic ports.
stories.why: Russia is a primary global producer and exporter of crude oil, supplying major international energy markets via sea-borne routes.

stories.headline: Nigeria: the financial stakes behind the appointment of Stanley Amuchie as head of Fidelity Bank
stories.summary: Fidelity Bank Plc confirmed Stanley Chiedoziem Amuchie as chief executive, starting 1 January 2027 after approval from the Central Bank of Nigeria. He succeeds Nneka Onyeali-Ikpe, whose term ends 31 December 2026.
stories.why: Fidelity Bank is a Nigerian commercial lender, and leadership transitions at listed banks can influence strategy, lending and investor perception.
stories.original_headline: Nigeria : les enjeux financiers derrière la nomination de Stanley Amuchie à la tête de Fidelity Bank

stories.headline: Historic maximum. Cargo transportation via "Irkeshtam" exceeded 4 million tons
stories.summary: Freight volume through the Chinese side of the Irkeshtam crossing on the Kyrgyzstan border exceeded 4 million tonnes for the first time since the start of 2026. It is a record for the crossing.
stories.why: Irkeshtam is a land route linking China and Kyrgyzstan, so its freight volumes reflect trade flows between Central Asia and China. Rising cargo through border crossings is a signal of regional trade activity.
stories.original_headline: Исторический максимум. Грузоперевозки через «Иркештам» превысили 4 миллиона тонн

stories.summary: Wall Street advanced, with the Nasdaq up more than 7% after a sell-off in technology stocks the previous session. Nvidia shares jumped more than 30% following Jensen Huang's return as chief executive.
stories.why: The Nasdaq is heavily weighted toward large technology companies, so moves in leading AI chip stocks have an outsized effect on the index.

stories.headline: SpaceX Faces AI Compute Capacity Constraints
stories.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX is currently renting out computing power from its data centers to competitors, including Anthropic, which is reportedly hindering the company's own internal AI development efforts.
stories.why: SpaceX is a major private aerospace company, and its strategic allocation of capital and infrastructure is closely watched by investors in the space and AI sectors.

stories.headline: Russia accuses Estonia of hostile actions that are "about to trigger an open war"
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry accused NATO and EU member Estonia of hostile actions that are close to triggering open war. The accusation followed Estonia's announcement that it was closing its land border.
stories.why: Estonia borders Russia and is a NATO and EU member, so tensions on that frontier affect regional security, trade routes and defence spending.
stories.original_headline: Rusia acusa a Estonia de acciones hostiles que están "a punto de desencadenar una guerra abierta"

stories.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over child sexual abuse images created by Grok
stories.summary: Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX Super Intelligence Corp, led by Elon Musk, alleging the company benefited from a Grok AI feature that generates child sexual abuse material and without safeguards.
stories.why: SpaceX is a privately held aerospace and technology company led by Elon Musk, and state lawsuits over AI products raise regulatory and legal risks for the company.
stories.original_headline: Virginia y Oregón demandan a SpaceX por imágenes de abuso sexual infantil creadas por Grok

stories.headline: National chicken production will reach 25 million in December
stories.summary: President Luis Abinader said national chicken production could reach 25 million units in December. Government institutions have been instructed to prioritize buying Dominican products for Christmas assistance programs.
stories.why: Poultry is a core domestic food supply, and government procurement priorities affect local agricultural producers and food prices.
stories.original_headline: Producción nacional de pollos alcanzará 25 millones en diciembre

stories.headline: Authentic Brands Group Acquires O'Neill

stories.why: Authentic Brands Group is a major player in the retail and brand management space, frequently acquiring distressed or legacy brands to leverage its global licensing platform.

stories.summary: The Southern Ethiopia Regional Chamber of Commerce and a sectoral association signed a memorandum of understanding with Emirates Holidays in Addis Ababa. The deal aims to strengthen business and tourism ties between Ethiopia and the UAE.
stories.why: Emirates Holidays is a travel company linked to Emirates airline's tourism business, and such regional trade agreements can shape cross-border tourism and investment flows.

stories.why: Nvidia is the world's largest maker of AI accelerator chips, so its share price moves influence the broader technology sector and AI-linked indices.

stories.headline: China’s Deyu lands in Dar in mission to deepen diplomatic ties, upgrade TAZARA standards
stories.summary: China's Deputy Foreign Minister Miao Deyu arrived in Dar es Salaam for an official visit to deepen bilateral ties. Discussions are set to cover the upgrade of TAZARA railway standards.
stories.why: TAZARA is the Tanzania-Zambia railway financed by China, and its upgrade affects regional freight logistics for landlocked Zambia.

stories.headline: Mexican stock exchange rebounds after a streak of six sessions with losses
stories.summary: Mexican local indices rose sharply after a six-session losing streak, following Wall Street peers. The rally was driven by a surge in Nvidia shares.
stories.why: The S&P/BMV IPC is Mexico's benchmark stock index, and it tends to follow US equity moves through its large exporter and financial constituents.

stories.headline: Fortune Shoes declares no dividend for FY26 as it slips into loss
stories.summary: Fortune Shoes will pay no dividend for FY26 after slipping into a loss. Following the announcement, its share price fell 2.16% to close at Tk13.60.
stories.why: Fortune Shoes is a Bangladeshi footwear maker listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange, where dividends and earnings drive investor returns.

stories.headline: Lawmakers criticize Nvidia's decision to re-appoint Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.summary: A group of Washington lawmakers sharply criticised Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive. They said Congress should pass a law restricting US chip exports to China.
stories.why: Nvidia is the leading maker of AI accelerator chips, and US export controls on advanced chips to China directly affect its sales.

stories.headline: Growth of the tourism sector and review of Law 158-01
stories.summary: Enrique E. De Marchena Kaluche, a former president of the Dominican hotel and tourism association, argues that growth in the tourism industry requires updating the legislation that governs the sector. He also called for provisions protecting tourists' rights.
stories.why: Tourism is a major source of foreign currency and employment for the Dominican Republic, so changes to its governing rules affect hotel operators and the wider economy.
stories.original_headline: Crecimiento sector turístico y revisión Ley 158-01

stories.headline: VP calls on NEEC to oversee the consolidation of 75 economic funds into a single fund
stories.summary: Vice President Deogratius Ndejembi called on the National Economic Empowerment Council to oversee merging 75 economic empowerment funds and programmes into a single fund. The aim is to simplify access to capital and loan guarantees, especially for young people.
stories.why: Public economic empowerment funds channel government credit and loan guarantees to businesses and households, so consolidation changes how state-backed lending reaches borrowers.

stories.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russian Warship and Cargo Ship in Libya
stories.summary: Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian warship Merkury and hit a cargo vessel in the Libyan port of Benghazi. The operation represents Kyiv's first admitted strike in Libya along Russian oil transit routes.
stories.why: Libya's Mediterranean coastline serves as a key transit area for maritime trade routes carrying Russian crude oil to Asian markets.

stories.headline: Find out how you can access the Christmas Brisita
stories.summary: The Dominican government said it will deliver 2,753,781 Christmas bonuses of RD$1,500 through direct transfers and cards, as part of the Brisita Navideña programme.
stories.why: Large state cash transfers inject household spending into the domestic economy, particularly around the end-of-year holiday period.
stories.original_headline: Infórmate sobre cómo puedes tener acceso a la Brisita Navideña

stories.headline: TopGum Reports Record Q3 Revenue of $40 Million
stories.summary: TopGum reported record third-quarter revenue exceeding $40 million, a 37% year-over-year increase. The company raised its annualized revenue run rate to over $150 million, driven by growth in dietary supplements.
stories.why: TopGum is a player in the consumer health and supplement manufacturing sector, which has seen steady growth in demand.

stories.headline: Bulgaria to Miss EU Deficit Target
stories.summary: Minister for EU Funds Atanas Pekanov said Bulgaria will not meet the European Commission's requirement to bring its deficit below 3% of GDP this year. The government will keep its income and social policies despite the risk of an excessive deficit procedure.
stories.why: Breaches of EU fiscal targets can trigger excessive deficit procedures, which affect a member state's borrowing costs and EU funding.

stories.headline: Bringing creole corn, honey and cacao to new markets: can digital commerce pave the way for them?
stories.summary: Mexico's retail e-commerce reached 941,000 million pesos during 2025. Food producers would need constant supply, buyers and logistics to benefit from the market.
stories.why: Online retail growth shapes demand for logistics, payments and consumer goods, and is a useful indicator of the size of Mexico's digital consumer economy.
stories.original_headline: Llevar maíz criollo, miel y cacao a nuevos mercados: ¿Puede el comercio digital abrirles camino?

stories.why: Nvidia designs graphics processors and AI accelerators that are central to data-center spending, so leadership changes at the company are closely watched by investors.

stories.summary: The Mexican peso gained against the dollar after reaching a new low since June 2025. The dollar's broader strength reflects bets on further Federal Reserve interest rate increases.
stories.why: The peso is Mexico's currency and its moves affect inflation, import costs and returns on peso-denominated assets for foreign investors.

stories.headline: Rosatom eyes Africa after synchronising nuclear project with Bangladesh’s national power grid
stories.summary: Unit 1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, built by Rosatom, was synchronised with Bangladesh's national grid. The reactor reached 40% of rated power, and the first megawatts reached the power system.
stories.why: Rooppur is Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant, and its output is meant to ease chronic power shortages in a fast-growing economy.

stories.why: United Bank for Africa is a major pan-African lender headquartered in Lagos, and its expansion depends on cross-border banking rules. Foreign capital limits in Nigeria shape how Nigerian banks can grow across Africa.

stories.summary: US equity markets had their third-worst week in six years, according to the El Economista headline. The same front page also covered the capture of Chapo Isidro.

stories.headline: Increase of up to 13% in minimum wage forecast for 2027, would exceed 10,800 pesos per month
stories.summary: Companies and consultancies expect the general minimum wage in Mexico to rise between 12% and 13% in 2027, taking it above 10,800 pesos per month. A smaller adjustment is expected for the northern border zone.
stories.why: Minimum wage changes affect labour costs for employers and consumer spending across Mexico. They are a key input for inflation and wage forecasts.
stories.original_headline: Prevén incremento de hasta 13% al salario mínimo en 2027, superaría los 10,800 pesos mensuales

stories.headline: Morocco: S&P maintains OCP's 'BBB-' rating despite supply crisis
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings affirmed Moroccan phosphate and fertiliser producer OCP's BBB- rating with a stable outlook, saying the company can absorb pressures on its operations. S&P expects a deterioration in some metrics.
stories.why: OCP is a major global phosphate and fertiliser producer and a key state-linked company in Morocco, so its credit rating affects its borrowing costs.
stories.original_headline: Maroc : S&P maintient la note « BBB- » d’OCP malgré la crise des approvisionnements

stories.headline: IBF Extends Black Sea High-Risk Zone to Bulgarian and Romanian Coasts
stories.summary: The International Bargaining Forum has extended the Black Sea high-risk maritime zone to cover areas off Bulgaria and Romania, under a decision adopted on November 18. Seafarers under IBF agreements gain additional entitlements, including a bonus.
stories.why: The International Bargaining Forum sets pay and conditions for seafarers on many merchant vessels. Higher-risk classifications raise crew costs and can affect shipping insurance and freight rates.

stories.headline: Côte d'Ivoire: SIREXE closes with 4,913 billion FCFA in investment prospects
stories.summary: The SIREXE 2026 extractives and energy fair in Abidjan closed on November 22 with 4,913 billion CFA francs of investment intentions and 27 agreements signed. The fair was held under the presidency of the Ivorian government.
stories.why: Investment pledges in extractives and energy signal future capital flows into West Africa's mining and energy projects.
stories.original_headline: Côte d’Ivoire : Le SIREXE referme ses portes avec 4 913 milliards FCFA de perspectives d’investissement

stories.headline: Kenya: banks request postponement of new capital requirements to 2028
stories.summary: Kenya's commercial banks are asking the Central Bank of Kenya to postpone by one year, to January 2028, new capital rules for systemically important institutions. The banks say the delay would let them adapt without curbing lending.
stories.why: Capital requirements set how much equity banks must hold against their loans, which shapes lending capacity and bank profitability. The Central Bank of Kenya sets these rules for the country's lenders.
stories.original_headline: Kenya : les banques demandent un report des nouvelles exigences de fonds propres à 2028

stories.headline: Morocco: net assets of UCITS fall 0.28% at end of October 2026
stories.summary: Net assets under management of Moroccan collective investment schemes (OPCVM) stood at 817.90 billion dirhams at end-October 2026. That is down from 820.19 billion a month earlier, a decline of 0.28%.
stories.why: Collective investment schemes pool savings from households and institutions and are a gauge of asset flows in Morocco's financial sector. Changes in assets reflect both market performance and investor flows.
stories.original_headline: Maroc : l’actif net des OPCVM recule de 0,28 % à fin octobre 2026

stories.headline: Nigeria: Cornerstone Insurance becomes a holding company and separates its life and non-life activities
stories.summary: Nigeria's Cornerstone Insurance Plc is restructuring into a holding company and separating its life and non-life insurance businesses into distinct subsidiaries. The move aims to comply with Nigeria's 2025 insurance reform law, which requires the split.
stories.why: Cornerstone is a listed Nigerian insurer, and regulatory reforms are reshaping the country's insurance sector. Compliance restructuring can affect capital allocation and corporate structure.
stories.original_headline: Nigeria : Cornerstone Insurance devient une holding et sépare ses activités vie et non-vie

stories.headline: Govt secretaries barred from bank board appointments under new policy
stories.summary: New Bangladeshi rules bar government secretaries from bank board appointments. Chairpersons and directors will serve three-year terms, with consecutive terms capped at two.
stories.why: Board composition and governance rules at banks affect oversight, risk management and investor confidence in the banking sector.

stories.headline: Electronics exceed 10% of Mexico's manufacturing GDP for the first time since 2005
stories.summary: Electronic component manufacturing in Mexico grew 23.2% year on year in real terms, accounting for 61% of the electronics industry's gain in the third quarter of 2026. The sector's share of manufacturing output exceeded 10%.
stories.why: Mexico is a major manufacturing and export hub, so growth in electronics affects its trade balance and its appeal to multinational supply chains.
stories.original_headline: La electrónica supera 10% del PIB manufacturero de México por primera vez desde 2005

stories.headline: Libya’s eastern government suspects drone attack caused explosion
stories.summary: A suspected drone attack caused an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, the eastern-based government said. No group has claimed responsibility.
stories.why: Libya's oil output and shipping lanes are a major factor in global energy supply, and Russia's military presence there is part of wider Mediterranean geopolitics.

stories.headline: Pakistan Rice Exports Reach 1.35 Million Tonnes in First Four Months of FY27
stories.summary: Pakistan exported 1.35 million tonnes of rice during the first four months of fiscal year 2027. Increased foreign shipments contributed to domestic foreign exchange earnings.
stories.why: Rice is one of Pakistan's principal agricultural export commodities, generating key trade revenue.

stories.headline: Ventas minoristas de UK superaron las previsiones
stories.summary: UK retail sales rose 0.7% month on month in October, ahead of expectations.
stories.why: Retail sales are a key gauge of consumer spending, which drives a large share of UK economic growth.

stories.headline: The Remarkables Pauses Ski-Field Fast-Track Expansion Over Eco Concerns
stories.summary: The Remarkables ski area in New Zealand put its fast-track expansion application on hold following Department of Conservation warnings regarding permanent environmental impacts on local landforms.
stories.why: NZ Alpine ski resorts generate significant tourism revenue for New Zealand's South Island economy.

stories.headline: Tight Liquidity, Debt Rating of Buma (DOID) Subsidiary Plunges
stories.summary: PEFINDO downgraded the credit rating of PT Bukit Makmur Mandiri Utama (BOLD), a subsidiary of PT BUMA Internasional Group (DOID). The move was linked to tight liquidity, according to the headline.
stories.why: Credit rating downgrades raise borrowing costs for a company and its affiliates, and Buma is an Indonesian coal mining group.
stories.original_headline: Likuiditas Ketat, Peringkat Utang Anak Usaha Buma (DOID) Anjlok

stories.headline: Grand Theft Auto 6 Release Drives Record Traffic across Australia NBN Network
stories.summary: The launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 generated record data consumption across Australia's National Broadband Network as hundreds of thousands of users downloaded the game simultaneously.
stories.why: NBN Co operates Australia's wholesale national broadband infrastructure.

stories.headline: Pakistan Cabinet Approves SECP Amendment Bill to Overhaul Audit Oversight
stories.summary: The Pakistani Cabinet approved the SECP Amendment Bill 2026 after a tax task force flagged structural weaknesses in the current financial review framework, aiming to strengthen independent corporate auditing.
stories.why: The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan regulates capital markets and corporate governance in the country.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Fell Sharply During the Week
stories.summary: Oil prices fell sharply during the week. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to set production policy for 2027.
stories.why: OPEC+ coordinates output among major oil producers, so its production decisions directly influence global crude prices.
stories.why_moved: Oil fell sharply over the week, and the report links the outlook to OPEC+ ministers' meetings on November 29 that will set 2027 production policy.
stories.original_headline: Precios del petróleo cayeron fuerte durante la semana

stories.headline: Slow 5G Infrastructure Rollout Constrains Nigeria Digital Economy Growth
stories.summary: Inadequate coverage and inconsistent service in Nigeria's 5G network are hindering access to the country's $18 billion digital economy, according to market analyses.
stories.why: Nigeria is Africa's largest telecommunications market by subscriber count and a key hub for West African technology investments.

stories.headline: Marvell and Lumentum Shares Fall
stories.summary: Marvell Technology fell to $122, 63% below its all-time high. Lumentum has dropped 60% from its peak.
stories.why: Marvell designs custom chips for data centers and networking, and Lumentum makes optical components used in AI and cloud infrastructure, so both trade on AI-related demand sentiment.

stories.headline: New Zealand Delivery CEO Criticizes Tax Advantage enjoyed by Multinationals
stories.summary: The founder of a New Zealand domestic food delivery company stated that local businesses face a higher tax burden compared to global platforms like Uber Eats relative to revenues.
stories.why: Tax equity discussions affect market competition between international digital platforms and domestic small businesses.

stories.headline: Rupiah Opens at Rp 18.270 per US Dollar Today
stories.summary: The rupiah weakened 0.05% against the dollar at the start of the week. Expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike have eased, giving emerging-market currencies room.
stories.why: The rupiah is Indonesia's currency, and its level against the dollar is sensitive to US interest-rate expectations and capital flows.
stories.original_headline: Pagi Ini Rupiah Dibuka ke Rp 18.270 per Dolar AS

stories.headline: Bank of Tanzania to Regulate Zanzibar’s Non-Deposit-Taking Microfinance Providers
stories.summary: The Bank of Tanzania will regulate and supervise non-deposit-taking microfinance providers in Zanzibar, previously licensed by the Ministry of Finance. Existing providers must apply by 31 December 2026.
stories.why: Microfinance providers extend small loans to households and businesses; central-bank oversight sets capital and governance standards for the sector.

stories.headline: BSP seeks to open PH payment system to more players
stories.summary: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas is seeking industry feedback on a draft circular that would support clearing sponsorship and third-party arrangements. The aim is to avoid limiting access to institutions able to build their own infrastructure.
stories.why: The central bank oversees the Philippine payment system, and access rules affect competition among banks, fintechs and payment providers.

stories.headline: Turkey looks to shake PH trade ties out of ‘autopilot’
stories.summary: Turkey plans a series of business missions to push firms from both countries toward new deals. Turkey's ambassador to the Philippines said bilateral trade volume is very low.
stories.why: Bilateral trade and investment flows between mid-sized emerging economies can open export opportunities for firms in both countries. Turkey and the Philippines are both emerging markets.

stories.headline: BOC tightens tracking of container movements
stories.summary: The Bureau of Customs is expanding electronic surveillance of domestic cargo through GPS-based monitoring on designated routes for covered containers. Customs Memorandum Order No. 19-2026 aims to prevent smuggling.
stories.why: Customs enforcement affects import logistics, compliance costs and tax collection for importers and logistics operators.

stories.headline: Universal Robina eyes P 8-B capex in 2027, mostly for PH projects
stories.summary: Universal Robina plans up to P8 billion in capital expenditure in 2027, with 80-85% allocated to domestic projects. The spending will expand manufacturing capacity in the Philippines and Southeast Asia.
stories.why: Universal Robina is a major Philippine food and beverage manufacturer, and its capital spending indicates expansion plans and domestic investment.

stories.headline: Theft of Globe’s network assets almost doubled
stories.summary: Globe Telecom reported a 96% surge in network infrastructure theft through October 2026. Pilferage incident tickets reached 2,616, nearly doubling from 1,334.
stories.why: Globe is one of the Philippines' largest telecom providers, and network damage affects service reliability and repair costs.

stories.headline: Breaking! JCI Falls 1%, Here's the Cause
stories.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.04% to 5,092.68 at the start of trading. Market sentiment included the Indonesia-EU trade agreement.
stories.why: The IHSG is Indonesia's main stock benchmark, tracking the country's largest listed companies. Its moves reflect local investor sentiment and foreign flows.
stories.why_moved: The index opened lower amid market sentiment that includes the Indonesia-EU trade agreement, according to the report. The report does not give further detail on the cause.
stories.original_headline: Breaking! IHSG Turun 1%, Ini Penyebabnya

stories.headline: DOE insists on Semirara asset disclosure for ‘fair’ auction
stories.summary: Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the DOE will require Semirara Mining and Power to disclose detailed asset information before competitive bidding for the Semirara coal mine development contract. The current operating contract for the country's largest coal site is held by SMPC.
stories.why: Semirara is the Philippines' largest coal site and supplies power generation, so the contract's terms affect domestic coal supply and power costs.

stories.headline: Financing gaps hold back MSMEs from shift to clean energy
stories.summary: High upfront capital costs and elevated interest rates are preventing Philippine small and medium enterprises from adopting renewable energy, an OECD report found. It said 59% of surveyed MSMEs identified these barriers.
stories.why: Small and medium enterprises are a large share of employment in the Philippines, and their energy costs affect productivity and competitiveness.

stories.headline: Philippines Gasoline Prices Set for 3 Pesos per Liter Reduction
stories.summary: Retail fuel prices in the Philippines will drop by up to 3 pesos per liter starting November 24. The price cut marks the third consecutive weekly decline for gasoline and diesel.
stories.why: Domestic petroleum pricing in the Philippines impacts transport inflation and consumer expenditure.

stories.headline: US gov’t backs Cagayan to Davao subsea cable
stories.summary: The US Trade and Development Agency awarded a grant for a feasibility study of the Silangan Submarine Cable System. The 2,166-kilometer fiber network aims to support the Philippines' data center ambitions.
stories.why: Subsea cables carry most international internet traffic, and data center hubs depend on such connectivity.

stories.headline: South Africa Competition Watchdog Reviews Ticketpro Acquisition
stories.summary: The Competition Commission of South Africa is considering an investigation into the acquisition of ticketing firm Ticketpro. Regulatory provisions allow reviews of transactions below standard notification thresholds.
stories.why: The Competition Commission is South Africa's statutory antitrust regulator overseeing merger approvals and fair trade practices.

stories.headline: Mr Price Chief Executive Criticizes Software Changes at Durban Container Port
stories.summary: Retail group Mr Price's CEO expressed concerns over operational software modifications implemented at the Durban port terminal close to peak shopping season, warning of supply chain disruptions.
stories.why: Mr Price Group is a major South African value retailer dependent on smooth port operations for apparel and homeware imports.

stories.headline: Philippine hog stock falls to three-decade low
stories.summary: The Philippines' national swine inventory declined 1.9% to 8.94 million heads as of Sept. 30, its lowest level since 1995, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority. Structural headwinds are cited for domestic hog producers.
stories.why: Hog inventories drive domestic pork supply and prices, which feed into food inflation and the earnings of livestock and feed producers.

stories.headline: South African Mining Companies Seek Removal of RMA Board Chairman
stories.summary: Three major mining companies are pushing to remove Thabo Dloti as chairman of Rand Mutual Assurance. A shareholder vote on the governance matter is scheduled for December 11.
stories.why: Rand Mutual Assurance administers worker compensation benefits across South Africa's mining and industrial sectors.

stories.headline: Nigeria Projects Higher Crop Yields Across 13 Food Commodities in 2026
stories.summary: Nigeria's agricultural output forecast indicates increased harvest volumes for 13 major food crops during the 2026 wet season, boosting national food security prospects.
stories.why: Agriculture represents a vital economic sector in Nigeria, employing a large segment of the workforce and affecting domestic inflation.

stories.headline: Singapore to Grant Property Tax Rebates to Owner-Occupiers in 2027
stories.summary: Singapore announced a one-off property tax rebate for owner-occupied residential properties in 2027, offering a 15% rebate to HDB flat owners and a 10% rebate capped at S$100 for private homeowners.
stories.why: Singapore periodically uses targeted tax rebates to offset living costs for residential property owners.

stories.headline: Sanctions. Liquidation of OJSC "Processing KJ" announced in Kyrgyzstan
stories.summary: Kyrgyzstan is liquidating OJSC Processing KJ, which was placed under UK sanctions in October. The information was posted on the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange website.
stories.why: Sanctions can restrict a company's access to banking and payments; liquidation ends its operations, with consequences for counterparties in the region.
stories.original_headline: Санкции. В Кыргызстане объявлено о ликвидации ОАО «Процессинг КейДжи»

stories.headline: EBRD and Iraqi Private Banks League Discuss Expanding SME Financing Facilities
stories.summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development met with the Iraqi Private Banks League to explore expanding trade and SME credit lines. Separately, Iraq announced releasing $1 billion to pay outstanding contractor debts.
stories.why: Development bank credit lines increase liquidity access for private sector small businesses in post-conflict emerging economies.

entities.name: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

stories.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index fell 0.92% to 5,146.33, with foreign investors net selling Rp855 billion. The energy sector weakened.
stories.why: The IHSG is Indonesia's main equity benchmark, and foreign flows and sector moves affect the country's stock market valuations and currency.
stories.why_moved: Foreign investors were net sellers of Rp855 billion and the energy sector weakened, pressuring the index.

stories.summary: Asian stock markets weakened on Monday, led by the Kospi index, which fell 2.34%. Technology stocks were a drag on the market.
stories.why: The Kospi tracks South Korea's largest listed companies, including major semiconductor makers, so its moves reflect the country's tech-heavy market.

stories.headline: Operators jostle for market share after Uber’s exit
stories.summary: Following Uber's exit from Nigeria on September 2, 2026, Bolt, inDrive and Ona are competing for riders. Fares, safety and driver welfare are central to the contest.
stories.why: Uber is a global ride-hailing and delivery platform; its market withdrawals reshape competition and pricing for rivals in the markets it leaves.

stories.summary: Swiss specialty chemicals producer Clariant and private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice are in discussions to acquire US-based chemical company Ashland, according to Bloomberg reports.
stories.why: Ashland is a major US specialty chemicals company; corporate buyouts in the sector alter market consolidation and supply chain dynamics.

stories.headline: NELFUND reviews structure as student loan beneficiaries hit 870,000
stories.summary: NELFUND has begun an organisational review as its student loan scheme records about 870,000 beneficiaries and over N375bn in disbursements. The agency says there is no disruption.
stories.why: NELFUND is Nigeria's federal student loan agency; its disbursement levels reflect public spending on education financing.

stories.headline: Gold Rebounds From 14-Month Low on Safe-Haven Buying Amid Tech Rout
stories.summary: Gold prices rose up to 1.3% to around $3,582 per ounce, recovering from 14-month lows. Safe-haven demand increased as global technology stocks plunged and traders reduced bets on near-term Federal Reserve rate hikes.
stories.why: Gold is traditionally viewed as a safe-haven asset during times of equity market volatility and economic uncertainty.

stories.headline: 10 Stocks Most Sold by Foreign Investors as JCI Slumps
stories.summary: The IHSG fell for five consecutive sessions and lost 3.71% over the past week. Foreign investors were net sellers of ten listed stocks.
stories.why: The IHSG is Indonesia's main stock benchmark, and foreign flows often drive large swings in it. Persistent outflows can weigh on the rupiah and local equity valuations.
stories.why_moved: Foreign investors sold heavily, according to the report, and the index recorded a five-day losing streak. The report does not state a specific trigger.

stories.headline: Tower Records Japan Suffers Cybersecurity Breach Affecting 10.2 Million Accounts
stories.summary: Tower Records Japan confirmed a network intrusion exposed user login credentials, including email addresses and account IDs, for approximately 10.2 million registered accounts.
stories.why: Retail data breaches expose enterprises to liability liabilities, security upgrade expenses, and customer churn.

stories.headline: Coal emerges as leading power source as gas supply falters
stories.summary: Coal's share of total electricity generation rose from 6.24% in FY2021-22 to 26.72% in FY25, according to Bangladesh Power Development Board data.
stories.why: Bangladesh relies heavily on imported fuels for power, so shifts between coal and gas affect its energy costs and import bills.

stories.headline: ADC faults Tinubu’s call to forget fuel subsidy
stories.summary: The ADC Presidential Campaign Council accused President Tinubu of insensitivity after he urged Nigerians to forget the fuel subsidy removal and move on from the policy.
stories.why: Fuel subsidy removal changes pump prices and public finances in Nigeria, a major African oil producer, so political debate over it affects policy expectations.
